remainingBlockers.summary: roleConfig carries one key (releaseAuthorityPublicKey*) that verifies every per-request role-use token; the issuer is an unattended online attestor. The Node never sees a release object, so 'only the operator release authority can authorize a new generation; runtime cannot mint a release' has no cryptographic expression on the Node. Need key hierarchy decision (offline release key -> scoped online use key with cohort/generation/expiry) or explicit acceptance of a single trusted online key, plus rotation/revocation and the runtime->attestor request interface.

/v1/executions/receipts is bound to EXECUTION/MODEL business tokens, but at 72028 it is the CP observe/reconcile path (dispatch.py:339 observation_only=attempt.operation=='observe'; node_transport.py:83). No business token exists while fenced, after expiry or after generation change, so in-flight reconciliation, lost-response recovery and the B4 quiescence proof cannot read receipts. The 'separate typed safety authorization' for cancel/quarantine/receipts is not defined in the schema.

Post-release per-member readmission after a restart has no phase row, writer or fence rule (text: new operator-bound release transition; D4: no per-member readmission; releases bind all-five evidence). persistence-abi gives releases a 'short expiry' with no refresh rule: a new release needs five fresh members, so one unrelated offline worker would block steady state at release expiry, contradicting ADR100 selected-healthy. Owner predicate caps admissions at 120s (continuous attestor refresh; outage = deny all) and eligible(selected=[]) and eligible(selected=[0,0]) return True.

Writers are prose ('operator attestor', 'approval writer', 'guarded operator CAS function') with no named DB principals, GRANT/function owners or separation rule (attestor must not hold planner/approval grants). persistence-abi contradicts itself (admissions 'FK ...release' vs 'no FK to an already existing release'). CP-side one-use nonce/evidence writes at commit need runtime INSERT, which conflicts with 'runtime read/lock only' unless those tables are classified as non-authority runtime-writable with distinct grants.
